input.summary:
Kitchen interior (parts/room-2.mjs): a galley along the north wall (fridge, white counter with sink, hob and oven, spruce trapdoor cabinets), a quartz-capped breakfast bar at z=12 with birch-stair stools at z=13, and an orange rug, all inside [11,2,9,15,4,13]. Three hung lanterns under the beams; the room lights 10-15 at the feet with no dark or dim cells, and the walk check is OK.
make.sh builds the whole house with 22 kitchen blocks placed and no refused writes or off-palette blocks. Elements item 29 ticked in elements.md.
Lanes stay open: x=15 at z=9..10 to the gallery, the z=10 aisle from the utility door, and x=11 and x=15 along z=11..13 to dining.
left: The terrazzo floor is laid by the shell (y=1), so this part writes no floor; that matches the plan's ownership.
The walk check reports 2 cells unreached at y=4 (13,4,9 and 13,4,12). They are headroom above the cabinet and bar, not floor cells, so the verdict is OK.
The stools are birch stairs and read as light blocks at a glance; a dark stair or a trapdoor seat was not tried.
Floating-block warnings in build check come from the roof and beam parts (x=14..21 at y=5), not from this room.

waste.what: Looked up how the galley_kitchen helper lays out its footprint (whether its counter row would block the gallery lane), then drew the kitchen by hand as layers() rows instead of calling it.
waste.cost: One source read of h3.mjs and about 3 minutes of deciding the lanes by hand.
waste.tool: A footprint preview for vocab helpers, e.g. `mcd plan --helper galley_kitchen` printing the cells it would fill and which room lanes it cuts, so a designer can pick a helper without reading its source.

waste.what: The first make.sh failed because layers() is not exported from vocab.mjs (it lives in the build library), which cost a rebuild cycle.
waste.cost: One failed make.sh run and one import fix.
waste.tool: vocab.mjs should re-export layers() (and the other build-library helpers designers use), so every part imports from one place.

waste.what: Chose the state value form (strings like "false" and "south") by guessing from the examples and checking the output afterwards.
waste.cost: No retries, but it was a guess with no check before the build.
waste.tool: A `mcd states`-based validator run inside layers() or as a pre-build lint, which would flag wrong state values and boolean/string mismatches before make.sh.

waste.what: Checked the lantern spots and the dim cells by reading the room check output, then placed a third lantern by hand from its suggestion.
waste.tool: `mcd room --apply-lamps` or a lamp-placement helper that writes the suggested lantern spots into the part, so the light pass needs no second build.
